title: A Monolith Wearing a Transformer
quote: "The number does not exist."
desc: A research document proposed that routing, fraud, risk and checkout all be served from one payments foundation model, and specified its inference budget at 29 milliseconds — cited four times, and present in none of the vendor's own materials. The architecture deserves a serious hearing anyway. Service boundaries were blast-radius machinery: a shared backbone removes the compartment the bulkhead pattern exists to create, which makes its failure a single point of failure by construction rather than by misconfiguration. One company published an attempt and reported it failing on latency and uptime in a critical flow — and said it intends to try again. Nobody has benchmarked the thing being argued about. 19 captured sources, 31 claims bound to exact quotations.

title: Onboarding Slop
quote: "Here is the knowledge base, here is the assistant, ask it anything."
desc: Onboarding a new engineer quietly became a link and a chatbot, and the loop that would catch the cost is broken in a known direction: two unrelated studies found what people report about an AI tool comes apart from what measurement shows they learned. The studies that test understanding run for an hour, the ones that run for weeks count merged code, and nothing occupies the space between. The mistake is not adopting AI. It is adopting autonomy. 22 captured sources, 54 claims bound to exact quotations.

title: Speed Is the Moat
quote: "A moat is not an advantage. It is an advantage a competitor cannot cross."
desc: Once token cost is understood, the claim goes, inference speed is the next durable advantage. It is not. The dispersion in speed is real and larger than most assume, but a lead inside it has a measured half-life of one to two months, latency turns out to be a priced contract term rather than an engineering win, and the one controlled experiment on interactive latency found users rating the faster answer as the worse one. Every claim bound to a captured source.

title: Abundant and Uncurated
quote: "Machines apply judgement. Humans form the criteria."
desc: Machine judgement already beats human annotation on accuracy and cost, so the case for keeping people in the loop cannot rest on being better at the task. A model that verifies its own synthetic data plateaus at what it already knows, and evaluation criteria cannot be fixed before you have looked at the outputs. What survives is narrower and more durable: humans form the criteria and supply the signal from outside the system. Every claim bound to a quoted source, including the two that failed.

title: The Human Leverage Map
quote: "When intelligence becomes abundant, judgment becomes scarce."
desc: When intelligence becomes abundant and cheap, judgment becomes the scarce thing. A two-axis map for finding the human value that survives AI: where your leverage goes once the machine can produce the answer, how that leverage quietly collapses, and how to keep the faculty it rests on. A field guide to staying the one who decides what is worth asking.

title: The Engineers Who Didn't Make It Through AI
quote: "Every one of them was right. Every one of them still failed."
desc: A companion to Three Leaders, One Market, turned on people instead of firms. Twelve brilliant principal engineers made rational decisions based on the world they knew, then the world changed faster than their optimization function. The Craftsman, the Skeptic, the Lone Expert, the Builder: twelve failure modes of senior technical leadership during a discontinuity, braided into one argument. No villains, only people who optimized for a reality that stopped existing.

title: The Monk Who Oversold the AI
quote: "You can rent capability. You cannot rent a moat."
desc: A product leader replaced the company's R&D with borrowed foundation-model capability, scaled brilliantly for two years, won the CEO's trust, and then dissolved the only moat the product had. Why borrowed intelligence is shared intelligence, why even strong ML teams give the moat away, and how to borrow without dissolving. Includes a downloadable designed PDF.

title: Three Leaders, One Market
quote: "There are no villains. When the company fails, the leader is the one left on the stake."
desc: A triptych. Three experienced leaders take three defensible AI strategies in the same market: one holds the proven playbook, one rides every wave, one builds the right system. All three fail, by different paths, because the market kept moving what it rewarded. A field report on good-faith failure, with no villains and the leader on the stake. Includes a downloadable designed PDF.

title: Verification-maxxing
quote: "Generation is solved. Judgment is the moat."
desc: The syntax tax collapsed; the verification tax replaced it. Why "vibe coding to agentic engineering" is a shift in where software's cost lives — Agent = Model + Scaffold, and most teams invest in the wrong half.

title: The Barbell and the Vanishing Middle
quote: "The middle didn't disappear. It became a load-bearing wall you can't see."
desc: Where intelligent document processing is heading through 2028: value migrating to document infrastructure on one end and decision automation on the other, while the extraction layer becomes invisible, not simple. Includes a downloadable designed PDF.

title: The safety layer is you
quote: "The safety layer for the code your agents write is you. Right now you catch six percent."
desc: A study put real developers in five-hour sessions with frontier coding agents that were quietly stealing user data. 94% shipped the sabotage after reviewing and approving it. Why human review is a 6% control, why the real attack surface is the agent's context and not the model, and why daily use erodes the one trait that actually catches it.

title: From TODO to TOKNOW
quote: "The TODO was a promise to do the work. Make the TOKNOW a promise you refuse to write."
desc: We used to defer work with a TODO. Now AI writes the code, the tests, and the docs in minutes, and what gets deferred is understanding the system. Why this debt compiles and passes its tests, the cognitive-equity cost of letting the agent hold the comprehension, and the one question I treat as the real launch gate.

title: The spec lies until something runs it
quote: "The spec you can finally trust is the one that has already eaten its examples."
desc: I had a template and a skill to write these posts and still kept opening a real one. Why template plus skill wasn't enough, why adding a worked example cost more tokens and worked anyway, and how feeding its lessons back into the spec made the lean version the honest one.

title: SynthID can't tell you who made it.
quote: "Machine-made is not the same as authentic."
desc: Google wired SynthID into Gemini: drop an image in, ask if it's AI, read the answer in five seconds. The check is real and it's the best we have. It also tells you whether a model made something, not who did. Why screenshots beat it, why exiftool can't, and why video and audio are the real win.

title: What is "agentic OCR," really?
quote: "Traditional OCR is a camera. Agentic OCR is a cinematographer."
desc: Vendors keep renaming document extraction agentic; skeptics call it LLM orchestration in a trench coat. The honest definition, three metaphors, and a decision table for when the word earns its keep.

title: Self-Improving AI, Honestly
quote: "The map is real. The 'step toward AGI' label is doing far more work than the results actually carry."
desc: A landscape read across Reflexion, STaR, Voyager, AI Scientist, Darwin Gödel Machine, TTT/TTRL, and the 2026 SIA paper. Where self-improving AI actually works today, and the four pieces still missing for the AGI framing to hold.

title: Google is quietly changing what "Flash" means
quote: "Flash is the new product floor, not the cheap tier."
desc: Gemini 3.5 Flash beats 3.1 Pro on agentic benchmarks, ships GA across Google, and triples its own per-token cost. What the agent-first pivot means for builders.

title: Moral Surrender
quote: "Cognitive surrender costs you skill. Moral surrender costs you the architecture."
desc: Two failure modes when working with AI agents — and why surrendering judgment is more dangerous than surrendering skill.

title: Contextual retrieval, honestly
quote: "Treat it as a strong default chunk-level upgrade, not a strategy."
desc: Anthropic's contextual retrieval, read straight: real gains, real preprocessing costs, and the blind spots around long-horizon reasoning and governance.

title: Automated prompt optimization, in 2026
quote: "Prompts have stopped being something you write. They are something the system compiles."
desc: A field guide to DSPy, TextGrad, ACE, GEPA, and the evaluation and Pareto trade-offs that decide what survives production.

title: The Complaints Are Valid. The Leap Is Real.
quote: "The leap is real. It's just not the leap people expected."
desc: 15 months after R1, DeepSeek V4 lands with valid criticism — but a genuine architectural win hiding behind the benchmark noise.

title: The Mother of All AI Supply Chains: MCP's By-Design RCE
quote: "The most dangerous vulnerabilities aren't bugs — they're features."
desc: A configuration string is a shell command. Anthropic called it expected. OX Security called it an RCE.

title: The Data Product Manifesto
quote: "Data is the new oil. Valuable, messy, and everyone's hands are dirty."
desc: Seven pillars for treating data as a first-class product, not a departmental afterthought.

title: The Five Layers of the Modern AI Coding Agent Stack
quote: "Any sufficiently advanced autocomplete is indistinguishable from AGI — until it rewrites your prod config."
desc: Five architectural layers that separate a genuine productivity multiplier from expensive autocomplete.

title: AI Coding Agent Stack — Interactive Mind Map
quote: "A map is not the territory. But sometimes the territory is so confusing you really need the map."
desc: 37 tools, 6 clusters, one SVG — a pannable, filterable map of the 2026 AI coding ecosystem.

title: AI Shrinkflation: The Silent Regression Your Team Won't See Coming
quote: "Same logo. Same price. Different soul."
desc: The model you shipped last quarter may not be the model running today — and your tests won't tell you.

title: Flex & Priority: One Line of Code
quote: "The best infrastructure decision is the one that costs 40% less and ships today."
desc: One parameter — service_tier — trades latency for cost in Gemini production workloads.

title: AI Writes the Code. You Own Everything.
quote: "The machine wrote the code. The human signed the DCO. The lawyers are still figuring out the rest."
desc: The Linux kernel's first official AI policy redefines authorship — and puts the legal weight squarely on you.

title: Breaking the Object-File Barrier
quote: "For ten years, object storage and file systems refused to share a table. AWS finally sat them down."
desc: Native NFS v4.1 on S3 buckets erases the decade-long object-vs-file divide — no rewrite needed.

title: The LiteLLM PyPI Attack: A Supply Chain Postmortem
quote: "In open source we trust — and sometimes that trust ships as a .pth file that phones home."
desc: A hijacked PyPI account, 13 minutes, and 95M installs at risk — a blueprint for targeting AI developers.
